channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Oracle Projects $30 Billion Free Cash Flow in Fiscal 2029
item.description: Oracle Corp. gave a long-term outlook for free cash flow that was better than analysts’ estimates, easing investor nerves about the potential payoff from its artificial intelligence spending.
item.dc:creator: Brody Ford

item.title: AI Boom Complicates Fed’s Demand Versus Supply Call, Clarida Says
item.description: Former Federal Reserve Vice Chairman Richard Clarida says the Fed is weighing whether AI-driven growth represents a demand shock, which could call for higher rates, or whether productivity gains will eventually boost supply and ease inflation. He speaks on "Bloomberg Surveillance: The Fed Decides." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investors Eye AI Payoff in Microsoft, Alphabet Earnings
item.description: Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down expectations for Microsoft and Alphabet, which both report earnings after the bell, with Wall Street looking for proof that their massive AI investments are paying off. Plus, Bloomberg reports that Anthropic has tapped JPMorgan to lead the US retail offering for its potentially record-setting IPO. And, Apple is betting consumers will pay even more for a MacBook Pro with touch screens coming for the first time. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Weighs Offering 15%-20% of IPO to Retail Investors
item.description: Anthropic is weighing a retail offering of 15% to 20% of the shares available in the IPO, according to people familiar with the matter. Those sources say the company behind Claude has tapped JPMorgan Chase to lead the US retail offering. Bloomberg’s Ryan Gould discusses the plans with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Data Center Anger Is From the ‘Fringes,’ Host Digital Chair Says
item.description: Anger over the AI buildout is coming from the “fringes,” says Shawn Matthews, chairman of Host Digital, a vertically integrated data center developer. Matthews, who is the former CEO of Cantor Fitzgerald, argues the way to avoid backlash over data centers is to build in places that have the right space and power to support them. He speaks with Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Can Unlock More Creativity in Video Games, Says Ex-EA Executive
item.description: AI will help boost video game quality, allowing developers to be more creative and deal with issues like old code, says Bing Gordon, a founding executive at Electronic Arts and former chief product officer at Kleiner Perkins. He joins Ed Ludlow on “Bloomberg Tech" to discuss his new book, "Everybody Wins: What Games Teach Us About Making Products People Love." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Palantir’s Defense Chief Sees Chinese Threat to Taiwan Over AI
item.description: Palantir Technologies Inc.’s head of defense Mike Gallagher is warning that advances in artificial intelligence capabilities have made it more compelling for Chinese leader Xi Jinping to seize control of Taiwan, a chipmaking hub that has helped fuel the global AI boom.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Eastland

item.title: Countdown to Fed, Tech Earnings
item.description: Get a jump start on the US trading day with Dani Burger on "Bloomberg Open Interest." Powerful profits from SK Hynix refuel the AI trade as booming demand for memory chips shows no signs of slowing. Microsoft and Alphabet gear up to report results on the busiest day of earnings season for the S&P 500. Plus, Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh takes the spotlight, with the Fed expected to hold rates today while keeping the door open to a December move. Nuveen Chief Investment Officer Saira Malik and Goldman Sachs Chief US Economist David Mericle break down the forces shaping the market outlook through the rest of 2026. Plus, the view from Dallas with Causeway CEO Sarah Ketterer, DFW International Airport CEO Chris McLaughlin and Fortress Global Co-Head of Corporate Credit Brian Stewart. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple Unveils Touch-Screen MacBook Pro, Reversing Long-Held Jobs Stance
item.description: After two decades of spurning the idea, Apple Inc. unveiled an overhauled MacBook Pro that includes a touch screen, giving its flagship laptop a feature that has become a must-have in the personal computer industry.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Ransomware Negotiator Arrests Add Scrutiny to Shadowy Industry
item.description: Recent arrests are catching the attention of others in the cybersecurity industry.
item.dc:creator: Jordan Robertson

item.title: AI Fed Simulation Predicts Interest Rates Will Hold Steady
item.description: he Federal Reserve will decide whether to adjust the US's benchmark interest rate on Wednesday, with investment banks, economists, and journalists waiting to see if their predictions are correct. Researchers Tara Sinclair and Sophia Kazinnik have developed an AI simulation called Sim Fed, which uses AI agents to impersonate the 12 individuals who vote on interest rates, including "Sim Powell" and "Sim Cook". Bloomberg's Stacey Vanek Smith joins to break down what this means for the Fed. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Columbia Opens Claims for $16 Million Data Breach Settlement
item.description: Columbia University has opened the window for individuals impacted by the school’s data breach last year to claim part of a $16.1 million settlement.
item.dc:creator: Cameron Fozi

item.title: Microsoft, Alphabet Earnings Put Focus on AI Cash Flow Drain
item.description: Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc. shares have gone separate ways since the companies’ last earnings reports as Wall Street increasingly digs in on the way heavy artificial intelligence spending is weighing on corporate bottom lines. With the two technology giants and major AI players poised to post their results after the bell Wednesday, recent stock market trading indicates that investors give Microsoft an edge. We get a preview from Bloomberg Tech host Ed Ludlow. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Data-Center Borrowing May Test Credit Market: Fortress
item.description: Brian Stewart, global co-head of corporate credit at Fortress, says the credit market could face a more serious absorption problem from AI data-center borrowing. Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Stewart says that U.S. investment-grade issuance recently reached a record, while the AI funding cycle has so far been driven mainly by venture capital, growth equity and investment-grade bonds. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Robinhood Slides, Wendy's Rallies | Stock Movers
item.description:
Today's biggest winners and losers in the stock market.
On this episode of Stock Movers:
- Robinhood (HOOD) is declining after the brokerage reported third-quarter earnings per share that missed consensus estimates.
- Etsy (ETSY) shares are gaining after the online retail company reported third-quarter results that beat expectations on key metrics. It also announced that its CFO Lanny Baker will depart to pursue opportunities outside of Etsy.
- Wendy's (WEN) shares are moving higher on news Nelson Peltz's hedge fund Trian Fund Management is offering to buy the fast food chain for around $1.4 billion. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Causeway CEO Sees Opportunities in AI, Defense Stocks and French Banks
item.description: Sarah Ketterer, Causeway Capital Management CEO and fundamental portfolio manager, sees investment opportunities in aerospace and defense stocks. Speaking on "Bloomberg Open Interest," Ketterer also says "this is the time to accumulate French banks." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: UK Links Data Center Grid Access to Jobs, Local Investment
item.description: UK data centers used for critical services will be given priority access to the grid and the authority to generate power on site, under new rules aimed at speeding up construction of essential infrastructure.
item.dc:creator: Olivia Solon

item.title: Microsoft and Alphabet Earnings Put Focus on AI Cash Flow Drain
item.description: Microsoft Corp. and Alphabet Inc. shares have gone separate ways since the companies’ last earnings reports as Wall Street increasingly digs in on the way heavy artificial intelligence spending is weighing on corporate bottom lines.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Vlastelica

item.title: ASM Lifts 2027 Outlook as AI Buildout Fuels Demand For Tools
item.description: ASM International NV increased its revenue target for next year by about 24%, setting up the chip-equipment maker to hit its 2030 goal three years ahead of schedule after a surge in sales linked to AI investments.
item.dc:creator: Sarah Jacob

item.title: Anthropic Is More Reliant on Google, Amazon, Microsoft
item.description: Anthropic PBC is relying more and more on Alphabet Inc.’s Google, Amazon.com Inc. and Microsoft Corp. to sell its artificial intelligence technology to customers, despite the three companies being rivals, investors and key suppliers of computing power.
item.dc:creator: Davey Alba, Rebecca Torrence and Matt Day
